subject: Streaming API p99 spike during peak — Chatterly production incident
messages:
From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@chatterly.ai>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: alice.wu@chatterly.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Severe p99 latency spikes on /streaming/chat during peak — urgent

Hi Redwood support,

We're seeing sustained p99 spikes on the streaming chat endpoint (SSE) starting around 08:30 PDT during our morning peak. This started after the traffic jump from a campaign; p50 looks mostly okay but p95 and p99 have increased ~6x and our customer-side clients are timing out. We have multiple customer complaints and a priority internal incident.

Attached are a few request traces and a short sample request. Can you triage? We need ETA for mitigation and whether a rollback to earlier model variant will help.

Impact: production customers in the US; some chat sessions disconnecting; client-side reconnect thrash.

Thanks — Simon
Chatterly - Technical Ops

Attachments: p99_spike_traces.zip, sse-request-sample.json

From: support@redwood.com <support@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@chatterly.ai>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency spikes on /streaming/chat during peak — urgent

Hi Simon —

Thanks for the traces, we've opened an incident: JIRA-INC-3124. I've looped in Tessa and Marissa from the customer success / infra on-call. Can you confirm whether you're using the hosted API (api.redwood.ai) or a dedicated deployment? Also please share the client SDK version and any retries/backoff behavior.

We will prioritize triage and report back within 30 minutes.

— Redwood Support

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@chatterly.ai>, support@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency spikes on /streaming/chat during peak — urgent

Simon —

Thanks for flagging. Triage update: initial traces show a tail-latency cluster on connections routed to our us-west pool; can you confirm region? I'm escalating to infra (Sean) and the runtime owners (Markus on cc). If you are on hosted API, we may need to failover routing or temporarily shift to a lighter model variant.

Proposed immediate steps (we'll act once we have your confirmation):
- Snapshot current traffic and force-redirect a small percentage to us-east as a canary.
- If canary looks stable, increase routing and push fallback for all sessions.
- If routing isn't feasible quickly, roll models to a smaller variant and reduce max tokens for streaming until we stabilize.

Please confirm region and any customer deadlines for reconnects.

Tessa
Sr. Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, simon.lee@chatterly.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency spikes on /streaming/chat during peak — urgent

Quick infra note: we see elevated kernel queue times and increased connection churn for the us-west SSE nodes starting 08:28 PDT. GPU utilization is normal but the connection handling threads are spiking CPU due to many concurrent long-lived connections during the campaign burst. This is causing head-of-line delays for tail tokens.

Immediate mitigation options I can action now:
1) Increase worker threads on the us-west pool (risk: temporary OOM if memory pressure spiked) — low-risk for short window.
2) Shift 20% of incoming traffic to us-east (requires routing rule update, ~5–7 min rollout).
3) Enable prefix KV cache aggressively for active chat sessions to cut repeated context recomputation for reuse patterns (config change, near-zero risk).

I recommend 2 + 3. I'll stand up the routing change and enable KV cache if we get signoff.

— Sean

From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@chatterly.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: alice.wu@chatterly.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency spikes on /streaming/chat during peak — urgent

Tessa/Sean —

We are on the hosted API in us-west. Chatterly is ok with an east canary and enabling the more aggressive KV cache. Our primary concern is client reconnect surface; shifting traffic is acceptable so long as session affinity for active chats is preserved where possible. No hard customer SLA deadline beyond minimizing session loss — but this is high impact for our top-tier customers.

Please proceed with the 20% east shift and KV cache. Keep me posted on rollback criteria.

Simon

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: simon.lee@chatterly.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency spikes on /streaming/chat during peak — urgent

I took a look at kernel selection and runtime telemetry. Two observations:
- The recent kernel patch we rolled last week slightly reduced memory headroom under very high connection counts. Not the direct cause but makes worker-thread increases more brittle.
- The KV cache threshold defaults were conservative; enabling aggressive cache will reduce redundant attention compute for repeated prompts, which should directly reduce tail latency for long-lived sessions.

Plan I'll implement with Sean's coordination:
- Enable KV aggressive cache immediately (no code deploy).
- Apply routing rule to move 20% to us-east canary (monitor p99 and error rates for 10m).
- Revert kernel patch for the us-west pool if we see instability, as rollback is straightforward; preflight rollback readiness now.

I'll signal when changes are live.

— Markus

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@chatterly.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: alice.wu@chatterly.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency spikes on /streaming/chat during peak — incident update and next steps

Update for all — final status for today: actions taken at ~10:25 PDT:
- 20% of traffic routed to us-east Canary (no session-affinity break observed for the sampled customers).
- Aggressive KV cache enabled across us-west pool.
- Increased worker thread limit temporarily.

Observations after 2h: p95 returned to baseline within the canary; p99 for us-west improved by ~60% vs peak but remains ~1.8x baseline. Error rates dropped from 0.9% to 0.15%. Chatterly reports far fewer disconnects and is marking incident as mitigated for now.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Markus: evaluate kernel rollback impact and coordinate a staged rollback if safe (owner: markus.klein).
- Infra: conduct post-mortem to understand connection handling threshold (owner: sean.gallagher).
- CS/Customer: run a short monitoring window tomorrow during the same campaign cadence; keep Chatterly on-call for validation. (owner: tessa_morgan)

Simon — thank you for fast responses and for sharing traces; we'll keep this thread updated and push a longer incident writeup to the Drive link. If anything regresses overnight or you see client reconnect spikes, please escalate immediately to the pager.

— Tessa
Senior Customer Success, Redwood Inference
